title: Autonomous Codebase Maintenance with Ornith-1.5
business: Enterprise software teams managing massive, legacy code repositories.
problem: Manual refactoring and bug fixing in large codebases are time-consuming, often leading to developer burnout and high operational costs for routine maintenance.
solution: Deploying Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B-GGUF as a local agentic coding assistant allows teams to automate complex repository-wide tasks while keeping sensitive code within their own infrastructure.
steps: Provision a local server with sufficient VRAM to host the 35B parameter model.
Launch the model using an OpenAI-compatible server like llama-server to enable tool-calling.
Configure an agentic coding CLI to point to the local server endpoint.
Define specific repository tasks for the agent to execute autonomously.
outcome: Increased developer velocity by offloading repetitive maintenance tasks to an agent that understands large-scale code context.
limitation: The use of YaRN for context window extension can slightly hurt quality on ordinary-length inputs, requiring users to verify performance when switching between short and long-context tasks.

diagram.title: Local Agentic Coding Workflow
diagram.description: The flow of a coding task from the developer to the local model and back to the repository.

code.content:
# Example of initializing the client for local agentic tasks
from openai import OpenAI

# Point to the local server running the GGUF model
client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1", api_key="EMPTY")

# Requesting an agentic task
response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Refactor the legacy auth module."}]
)
code.explanation: This code demonstrates how to connect an OpenAI-compatible client to a locally deployed Ornith-1.5 instance to trigger agentic coding workflows.
